metadata.title: EU Artificial Intelligence Act — Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 — OSCAL Catalog

links.text: Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (Digital Omnibus on AI), in force 27 July 2026

roles.title: Provider of an AI system or general-purpose AI model
roles.description: As defined in Article 3(3) of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689.

roles.title: Deployer of an AI system
roles.description: As defined in Article 3(4) of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689.

roles.description: As defined in Article 3(6) of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689.

roles.description: As defined in Article 3(7) of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689.

metadata.remarks: Structural representation of the operator-facing obligations of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 as OSCAL controls, AS AMENDED by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (the Digital Omnibus on AI), which entered into force on 27 July 2026. Article numbers and titles follow the Official Journal text of 13 June 2024 and were verified on 2026-07-27; the amendment layer was verified against the Official Journal text of Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 on the same date. Controls carry both the current application date and, where the Omnibus moved it, the original one. Control statements are condensed restatements written for assessment use; they are not quotations and are not legal advice. Where a statement and the Official Journal text differ, the Official Journal text governs. Coverage is deliberately partial and the interaction between the deferred high-risk dates and the unchanged Chapter IX general date is recorded as unresolved rather than guessed: see docs/SCOPE.md and docs/AMENDMENTS.md.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The Regulation lays down harmonised rules for placing on the market, putting into service and using AI systems in the Union, prohibitions of certain AI practices, specific requirements for high-risk AI systems and obligations for their operators, harmonised transparency rules for certain AI systems, rules for general-purpose AI models, and rules on market monitoring, governance and enforcement.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Included for scoping completeness. Not an assessable obligation on its own; it establishes what the remaining controls govern.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Determine whether the organisation falls within territorial and personal scope: providers placing on the market or putting into service AI systems (or placing general-purpose AI models) in the Union irrespective of establishment; deployers established or located in the Union; and providers and deployers in third countries where the output produced by the AI system is used in the Union. Record any applicable exclusion (military/defence/national-security purposes, scientific research and development, purely personal non-professional use, and free and open-source components except where otherwise provided).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Scope determination is the first assessable step: every downstream obligation is conditional on it. Record the determination and its basis as evidence. Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 added Article 2(13), allowing the Commission to limit application of specified Annex I-related requirements by delegated act where the relevant Union harmonisation law provides equivalent protection. Do not assume that limitation applies: record and cite the currently applicable delegated act before excluding an obligation.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Apply the Regulation's definitions when classifying the organisation's role and its systems, in particular 'AI system', 'provider', 'deployer', 'importer', 'distributor', 'operator', 'placing on the market', 'putting into service', 'intended purpose', 'reasonably foreseeable misuse', 'safety component', 'substantial modification', 'serious incident', and 'general-purpose AI model'.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Role classification drives which profile applies. A single organisation may be provider for one system and deployer for another. Amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 with effect from 27 July 2026: definitions of SME and small mid-cap company (SMC) added, and the definition of 'safety component' rewritten. The rewritten safety-component definition feeds directly into Article 6 classification.

guidelines.prose: Organisation-defined. The Regulation sets no interval; select one proportionate to the rate of change in the deployed AI estate.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Take measures to support the development of AI literacy of staff and other persons dealing with the operation and use of AI systems on the organisation's behalf, taking into account their technical knowledge, experience, education and training and the context of use. Review those measures at least every {{ insert: param, aia-4_prm_1 }} and after a material change in the organisation's AI systems or their use.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Applicable since 2 February 2025. The obligation was AMENDED by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 with effect from 27 July 2026: the duty is now to 'take measures to support the development of' AI literacy, replacing the stronger original formulation ('ensure, to their best extent, a sufficient level of'). An assessment performed before that date measured against the original wording. Evidence: training records, role-scoped curricula, and a register of persons in scope.

controls.title: Processing of special categories of personal data for bias detection and correction

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Where special categories of personal data are processed for the purpose of ensuring bias detection and correction, process them only to the extent strictly necessary and subject to all of the following safeguards: bias detection and correction cannot be effectively fulfilled by processing other data, including synthetic or anonymised data; technical limitations on the re-use of the data are applied, together with state-of-the-art security and privacy-preserving measures; strict controls on and documentation of access are applied so that only authorised persons with appropriate confidentiality obligations can access the data; the data is not transmitted, transferred or otherwise accessed by third parties; the data is deleted once the bias has been corrected or the retention period has ended, whichever comes first; and the records of processing explain why the processing was strictly necessary and why other data could not adequately achieve the purpose.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Inserted by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, in force 27 July 2026. Paragraph 1 concerns providers of high-risk AI systems; paragraph 2 extends equivalent permission to providers and deployers of other AI systems and models, and to deployers of high-risk AI systems, where bias could affect health, safety or fundamental rights. Article 4a now contains the special-category-data permission and its safeguards; assess it alongside Article 10 rather than in isolation.

controls.title: Prohibition — harmful subliminal, manipulative or deceptive techniques

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Do not place on the market, put into service or use an AI system that deploys subliminal techniques beyond a person's consciousness, or purposefully manipulative or deceptive techniques, with the objective or effect of materially distorting the behaviour of a person or group by appreciably impairing their ability to make an informed decision, thereby causing or being reasonably likely to cause significant harm.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Do not place on the market, put into service or use an AI system that exploits vulnerabilities of a person or specific group due to their age, disability or a specific social or economic situation, with the objective or effect of materially distorting behaviour in a manner that causes or is reasonably likely to cause significant harm.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A provider shall not place on the market or put into service an AI system intended to generate or manipulate realistic intimate or sexually explicit material of an identifiable natural person without that person's freely given, specific, informed, unambiguous and explicit consent. The provider prohibition also covers a reasonably foreseeable and reproducible outcome where adequate technical safeguards are absent. A deployer shall not purposefully use an AI system for that generation or manipulation without the same consent.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Inserted into Article 5(1) by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 as point (ba), applicable from 2 December 2026. Article 5(1a) distinguishes the provider test (intended purpose, or a reasonably foreseeable and reproducible outcome without adequate safeguards) from the deployer test (purposeful use). The prohibition does not cover manipulation of material lawfully generated with the person's consent where the manipulation does not alter its sexual nature or meaning. Assess intended purpose, foreseeable output, safeguards, consent and actual use separately.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A provider shall not place on the market or put into service an AI system intended to generate or manipulate child sexual abuse material or a pornographic performance involving a child within the meaning of Directive 2011/93/EU. The provider prohibition also covers a reasonably foreseeable and reproducible outcome where adequate technical safeguards are absent. A deployer shall not purposefully use an AI system for that generation or manipulation, subject to any applicable 'without right' exception under national law.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Inserted into Article 5(1) by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 as point (bb), applicable from 2 December 2026. The definitions are those of Directive 2011/93/EU. Article 5(1b) distinguishes the provider test (intended purpose, or a reasonably foreseeable and reproducible outcome without adequate safeguards) from the deployer test (purposeful use). The scope of any 'without right' exception is determined by applicable national law.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Do not place on the market, put into service or use an AI system for the evaluation or classification of natural persons or groups over time based on their social behaviour or known, inferred or predicted personal or personality characteristics, where the resulting social score leads to detrimental or unfavourable treatment that is unjustified or disproportionate to the social behaviour or its gravity, or occurs in social contexts unrelated to the context in which the data was generated.

controls.title: Prohibition — individual criminal-risk prediction based solely on profiling

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Do not place on the market, put into service for this specific purpose, or use an AI system to make risk assessments of natural persons in order to assess or predict the risk of a natural person committing a criminal offence, based solely on profiling or on assessing personality traits and characteristics. This does not apply to AI systems used to support human assessment based on objective and verifiable facts directly linked to a criminal activity.

controls.title: Prohibition — untargeted scraping of facial images

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Do not place on the market, put into service or use an AI system that creates or expands facial recognition databases through the untargeted scraping of facial images from the internet or CCTV footage.

controls.title: Prohibition — emotion inference in the workplace and education

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Do not place on the market, put into service for this specific purpose, or use an AI system to infer emotions of a natural person in the areas of workplace or education institutions, except where intended to be put in place or into the market for medical or safety reasons.

controls.title: Prohibition — biometric categorisation inferring sensitive attributes

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Do not place on the market, put into service for this specific purpose, or use a biometric categorisation system that categorises individual natural persons on the basis of their biometric data to deduce or infer race, political opinions, trade-union membership, religious or philosophical beliefs, sex life or sexual orientation. This does not cover labelling or filtering of lawfully acquired biometric datasets, nor categorisation of biometric data in the area of law enforcement.

controls.title: Prohibition — real-time remote biometric identification in publicly accessible spaces for law enforcement

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Do not use a real-time remote biometric identification system in publicly accessible spaces for the purposes of law enforcement, save where and in so far as strictly necessary for one of the narrowly defined objectives in Article 5(1)(h)(i)-(iii) and subject to the safeguards, authorisation and notification conditions in Article 5(2)-(7).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Where a Member State authorises such use, the derogation conditions (prior judicial or administrative authorisation, fundamental-rights impact assessment, registration, notification of the market surveillance and data protection authorities) are themselves assessable and must be evidenced.

groups.title: Classification of AI systems as high-risk

controls.title: Classification rules for high-risk AI systems

choice: Annex III(1) — biometrics (remote biometric identification, biometric categorisation, emotion recognition)
Annex III(2) — critical infrastructure (safety components in digital infrastructure, road traffic, utilities)
Annex III(3) — education and vocational training
Annex III(4) — employment, workers management and access to self-employment
Annex III(5) — access to and enjoyment of essential private and public services and benefits
Annex III(7) — migration, asylum and border control management
Annex III(8) — administration of justice and democratic processes

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Determine and document whether an AI system is high-risk and record the Annex III use case(s), where applicable, using {{ insert: param, aia-6_prm_1 }}. Under Article 6(1) a system is high-risk where it is intended to be used as a safety component of a product, or is itself a product, covered by the Union harmonisation legislation listed in Annex I AND is required to undergo a third-party conformity assessment under that legislation. Under Article 6(2) an AI system falling under one of the Annex III use cases is high-risk, unless the derogation in Article 6(3) applies and the provider documents its assessment before placing on the market or putting into service.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The current application dates are 2 December 2027 for Article 6(2) Annex III systems and 2 August 2028 for Article 6(1) Annex I product systems. Under new Article 6(1a), assistance, efficiency, convenience or quality-control functions that are unrelated to product safety are not treated as safety components, unless failure or malfunction could endanger health or safety. Under Article 6(1b), a third-party assessment performed solely for risks unrelated to health or safety does not satisfy Article 6(1)(b). Article 6(1c) preserves the sectoral definition of a safety component where one exists. Where the Article 6(3) derogation is relied on, retain the documented assessment and register the system under Article 49(2).

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Ensure the high-risk AI system complies with the requirements of Chapter III Section 2, taking into account its intended purpose and the generally acknowledged state of the art. Where a product is also subject to other Union harmonisation legislation listed in Annex I Section A, ensure consistency and avoid duplication by integrating this Regulation's requirements into that legislation's documentation and procedures.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The umbrella requirement: an assessment that finds every individual requirement satisfied but no coherent demonstration of overall compliance has not satisfied Article 8. Application date DEFERRED by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744: the obligations of stand-alone high-risk AI systems under Annex III now apply from 2 December 2027 (previously 2 August 2026), and for AI systems embedded in products covered by the Annex I harmonisation legislation from 2 August 2028 (previously 2 August 2027).

guidelines.prose: Organisation-defined. Article 9 requires 'regular systematic review' without fixing an interval; select one proportionate to the system's risk profile and rate of change, and shorten it on material change or after a serious incident.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Establish, implement, document and maintain a risk management system for the high-risk AI system as a continuous iterative process planned and run throughout its entire lifecycle, requiring regular systematic review and updating. The process comprises identification and analysis of known and reasonably foreseeable risks to health, safety and fundamental rights; estimation and evaluation of risks in intended use and under reasonably foreseeable misuse; evaluation of risks emerging from post-market monitoring data; and adoption of appropriate and targeted risk management measures. Review and update the risk management system at least every {{ insert: param, aia-9_prm_1 }}.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Testing (Article 9(6)-(8)) is part of this control: define ex-ante metrics and probabilistic thresholds, test against them, and retain results. Where persons under 18 or other vulnerable groups may be affected, Article 9(9) requires specific consideration. Application date DEFERRED by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744: the obligations of stand-alone high-risk AI systems under Annex III now apply from 2 December 2027 (previously 2 August 2026), and for AI systems embedded in products covered by the Annex I harmonisation legislation from 2 August 2028 (previously 2 August 2027).

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Where the high-risk AI system involves training of AI models with data, develop it on the basis of training, validation and testing data sets that meet the quality criteria of Article 10(2)-(4). Apply data governance and management practices covering design choices, data-collection processes and data origin, preparation operations, formulation of assumptions, assessment of availability quantity and suitability, examination for possible biases affecting health safety or fundamental rights, appropriate measures to detect prevent and mitigate those biases, and identification of relevant data gaps. Data sets shall be relevant, sufficiently representative, and to the best extent possible free of errors and complete in view of the intended purpose.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 deleted Article 10(5). The permission to process special categories of personal data for bias detection and correction, and its safeguards, now sit in Article 4a. Evidence includes data-provenance records, bias-assessment reports, documented data gaps and, where Article 4a is used, the required records explaining strict necessity and why other data were inadequate. The current high-risk application dates are 2 December 2027 for Annex III and 2 August 2028 for Annex I product systems.

guidelines.prose: Organisation-defined. Article 11 requires the documentation be 'kept up to date'; select a review interval and additionally trigger review on every substantial modification.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Draw up technical documentation for the high-risk AI system before it is placed on the market or put into service and keep it up to date. The documentation shall contain at least the elements set out in Annex IV and shall demonstrate compliance with the requirements of Chapter III Section 2, in a form enabling national competent authorities and notified bodies to assess that compliance. Review it at least every {{ insert: param, aia-11_prm_1 }} and after every substantial modification.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: SMEs including start-ups may supply the Annex IV elements in the simplified form provided for in Article 11(1). Evidence: the Annex IV document set with version history. Application date DEFERRED by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744: the obligations of stand-alone high-risk AI systems under Annex III now apply from 2 December 2027 (previously 2 August 2026), and for AI systems embedded in products covered by the Annex I harmonisation legislation from 2 August 2028 (previously 2 August 2027). Amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, with the amendment applicable from 2 August 2026: SMEs and small mid-cap companies may supply the Annex IV elements using a simplified template to be provided by the Commission. The underlying documentation obligation itself applies from the deferred high-risk date.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Design and develop the high-risk AI system so that it technically allows for automatic recording of events (logs) over its lifetime. Logging capabilities shall enable recording of events relevant to identifying situations that may result in the system presenting a risk within the meaning of Article 79(1) or in a substantial modification, to facilitating post-market monitoring, and to monitoring operation as required by Article 26(5). For Annex III(1)(a) systems, logging shall at minimum record the period of each use, the reference database against which input data has been checked, the input data for which the search led to a match, and the identification of the natural persons involved in verifying the results.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Article 12 is the design-time capability; Article 19 is the retention duty. Assess both or neither conclusion is safe. Application date DEFERRED by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744: the obligations of stand-alone high-risk AI systems under Annex III now apply from 2 December 2027 (previously 2 August 2026), and for AI systems embedded in products covered by the Annex I harmonisation legislation from 2 August 2028 (previously 2 August 2027).

controls.title: Transparency and provision of information to deployers

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Design and develop the high-risk AI system so that its operation is sufficiently transparent to enable deployers to interpret its output and use it appropriately. Accompany it with concise, complete, correct and clear instructions for use in an appropriate digital or other format, including the provider's identity and contact details, the system's characteristics capabilities and limitations of performance (intended purpose, accuracy robustness and cybersecurity levels, known and foreseeable circumstances that may lead to risks, technical capabilities relevant to explaining output, performance on specific persons or groups, input-data specifications), any predetermined changes, the human-oversight measures, required computational and hardware resources and expected lifetime, and a description of the logging mechanisms.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Application date DEFERRED by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744: the obligations of stand-alone high-risk AI systems under Annex III now apply from 2 December 2027 (previously 2 August 2026), and for AI systems embedded in products covered by the Annex I harmonisation legislation from 2 August 2028 (previously 2 August 2027).

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Design and develop the high-risk AI system, including with appropriate human-machine interface tools, so that it can be effectively overseen by natural persons during the period it is in use. Oversight measures shall be commensurate with the risks, level of autonomy and context of use, and shall enable the overseeing person to understand the system's capacities and limitations and monitor its operation, to remain aware of automation bias, to correctly interpret output, to decide not to use the system or to disregard, override or reverse its output, and to intervene or interrupt operation through a stop button or similar procedure allowing the system to halt in a safe state.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: For Annex III(1)(a) remote biometric identification, Article 14(5) additionally requires that no action or decision be taken on the basis of the identification unless separately verified and confirmed by at least two natural persons with the necessary competence, training and authority, with narrow exceptions. Application date DEFERRED by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744: the obligations of stand-alone high-risk AI systems under Annex III now apply from 2 December 2027 (previously 2 August 2026), and for AI systems embedded in products covered by the Annex I harmonisation legislation from 2 August 2028 (previously 2 August 2027).

guidelines.prose: Organisation-defined. Article 15(3) requires the metric to be declared in the instructions for use; it does not prescribe which metric.
Organisation-defined. The Regulation prescribes no numeric floor; the threshold must be appropriate to the intended purpose and consistent with what is declared under Article 13.
Organisation-defined. Select an interval proportionate to the threat model and rate of model or data change.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Design and develop the high-risk AI system to achieve an appropriate level of accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity and to perform consistently in those respects throughout its lifecycle. Declare the levels of accuracy and the relevant accuracy metrics in the instructions for use. Ensure resilience against errors, faults and inconsistencies, including through technical redundancy where appropriate; where the system continues to learn after being placed on the market or put into service, eliminate or reduce as far as possible the risk of biased outputs influencing future operations (feedback loops). Ensure resilience against attempts by unauthorised third parties to alter use, outputs or performance by exploiting vulnerabilities, including measures addressing data poisoning, model poisoning, adversarial examples, model evasion, confidentiality attacks and model flaws. Declared accuracy shall be at least {{ insert: param, aia-15_prm_2 }} on the metric {{ insert: param, aia-15_prm_1 }}, verified at least every {{ insert: param, aia-15_prm_3 }}.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Cybersecurity measures under Article 15(5) must be appropriate to the circumstances and risks; the Commission may encourage harmonised standards and common specifications, and conformity with those confers presumption of conformity under Article 40. Application date DEFERRED by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744: the obligations of stand-alone high-risk AI systems under Annex III now apply from 2 December 2027 (previously 2 August 2026), and for AI systems embedded in products covered by the Annex I harmonisation legislation from 2 August 2028 (previously 2 August 2027). Amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744: compliance with the cybersecurity requirements of the Cyber Resilience Act is deemed to satisfy the cybersecurity requirement of Article 15 (new Article 42(3)). Where that route is relied on, the CRA evidence is the evidence for this control.

groups.title: Obligations of providers and deployers of high-risk AI systems and other parties

controls.title: Obligations of providers of high-risk AI systems

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Providers of high-risk AI systems shall discharge each of the following obligations.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: ensure the system complies with the requirements of Chapter III Section 2

parts.name: item
parts.prose: indicate on the system, or where not possible on its packaging or accompanying documentation, the provider's name, registered trade name or trade mark and contact address

parts.name: item
parts.prose: have a quality management system in place complying with Article 17

parts.name: item
parts.prose: keep the documentation referred to in Article 18

parts.name: item
parts.prose: keep the automatically generated logs referred to in Article 19 when under the provider's control

parts.name: item
parts.prose: ensure the system undergoes the relevant conformity assessment procedure under Article 43 before being placed on the market or put into service

parts.name: item
parts.prose: draw up an EU declaration of conformity in accordance with Article 47

parts.name: item
parts.prose: affix the CE marking in accordance with Article 48

parts.name: item
parts.prose: comply with the registration obligations of Article 49(1)

parts.name: item
parts.prose: take the necessary corrective actions and provide information as required by Article 20

parts.name: item
parts.prose: upon reasoned request of a national competent authority, demonstrate conformity with the requirements of Chapter III Section 2

parts.name: item
parts.prose: ensure the system complies with accessibility requirements in accordance with Directives (EU) 2016/2102 and (EU) 2019/882

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: This control is a roll-up: each limb maps to a discrete control in this catalog (Articles 17, 18, 19, 20, 21, 43, 47, 48, 49). Assess the limbs, then assess that the roll-up is coherent. Application date DEFERRED by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744: the obligations of stand-alone high-risk AI systems under Annex III now apply from 2 December 2027 (previously 2 August 2026), and for AI systems embedded in products covered by the Annex I harmonisation legislation from 2 August 2028 (previously 2 August 2027).

guidelines.prose: Organisation-defined. Article 17 prescribes no interval; select one proportionate to the size of the organisation and the risk profile of its high-risk AI portfolio.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Put in place a quality management system ensuring compliance with this Regulation, documented in a systematic and orderly manner in the form of written policies, procedures and instructions. It shall include at least a strategy for regulatory compliance; procedures for design, design control and design verification; for development, quality control and quality assurance; for examination, test and validation before during and after development; technical specifications and standards applied; systems and procedures for data management; the risk management system of Article 9; setting up implementing and maintaining a post-market monitoring system under Article 72; procedures for reporting serious incidents under Article 73; handling communication with authorities; systems and procedures for record-keeping; resource management including security-of-supply measures; and an accountability framework. Review the quality management system at least every {{ insert: param, aia-17_prm_1 }}.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Providers already subject to a quality management system obligation under sectoral Union law may integrate these elements rather than duplicate them (Article 17(3)). Financial institutions subject to internal-governance requirements are presumed compliant for parts of this control (Article 17(4)). The current high-risk application dates are 2 December 2027 for Annex III and 2 August 2028 for Annex I product systems. Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 amended Article 17(2) so that the quality management system must be proportionate to the provider's size; this is the relevant proportionality rule for SMEs and small mid-cap companies.

constraints.description: Fixed by Article 18(1): a period ending 10 years after the high-risk AI system has been placed on the market or put into service. Not organisation-defined; may not be shortened.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Keep at the disposal of the national competent authorities, for a period of {{ insert: param, aia-18_prm_1 }} after the high-risk AI system has been placed on the market or put into service: the technical documentation of Article 11; the documentation concerning the quality management system; where applicable the documentation concerning changes approved by notified bodies; where applicable the decisions and other documents issued by notified bodies; and the EU declaration of conformity of Article 47.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Where the provider is established outside the Union, the authorised representative under Article 22 holds the corresponding duty. Application date DEFERRED by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744: the obligations of stand-alone high-risk AI systems under Annex III now apply from 2 December 2027 (previously 2 August 2026), and for AI systems embedded in products covered by the Annex I harmonisation legislation from 2 August 2028 (previously 2 August 2027).

constraints.description: Article 19(1) sets a floor of six months unless otherwise provided in applicable Union or national law. A longer period may be selected where the intended purpose requires it; a shorter period requires a legal basis.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Keep the logs automatically generated by the high-risk AI system under Article 12 to the extent such logs are under the provider's control, for a period appropriate to the intended purpose of the system and of at least {{ insert: param, aia-19_prm_1 }} unless provided otherwise in applicable Union or national law, in particular Union law on the protection of personal data.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Providers that are financial institutions subject to internal-governance requirements under Union financial-services law shall maintain the logs as part of the documentation kept under that law (Article 19(2)). Application date DEFERRED by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744: the obligations of stand-alone high-risk AI systems under Annex III now apply from 2 December 2027 (previously 2 August 2026), and for AI systems embedded in products covered by the Annex I harmonisation legislation from 2 August 2028 (previously 2 August 2027).

controls.title: Corrective actions and duty of information

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Where the provider considers or has reason to consider that a high-risk AI system it has placed on the market or put into service is not in conformity with this Regulation, immediately take the necessary corrective actions to bring the system into conformity, withdraw it, disable it, or recall it as appropriate, and inform the distributors, and where applicable the deployers, the authorised representative and the importers accordingly. Where the system presents a risk within the meaning of Article 79(1) and the provider becomes aware of it, immediately investigate the causes in collaboration with the reporting deployer where applicable and inform the market surveillance authorities competent for that system and, where applicable, the notified body, of the nature of the non-compliance and of any relevant corrective action taken.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Application date DEFERRED by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744: the obligations of stand-alone high-risk AI systems under Annex III now apply from 2 December 2027 (previously 2 August 2026), and for AI systems embedded in products covered by the Annex I harmonisation legislation from 2 August 2028 (previously 2 August 2027).

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Upon a reasoned request by a competent authority, provide that authority with all the information and documentation necessary to demonstrate the conformity of the high-risk AI system with the requirements of Chapter III Section 2, in a language which can be easily understood by the authority in an official Union language indicated by the Member State concerned. Upon reasoned request, give the requesting authority access to the automatically generated logs of the system to the extent those logs are under the provider's control. Keep any information obtained by an authority confidential in accordance with Article 78.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Application date DEFERRED by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744: the obligations of stand-alone high-risk AI systems under Annex III now apply from 2 December 2027 (previously 2 August 2026), and for AI systems embedded in products covered by the Annex I harmonisation legislation from 2 August 2028 (previously 2 August 2027).

controls.title: Authorised representatives of providers of high-risk AI systems

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Prior to making a high-risk AI system available on the Union market, a provider established in a third country shall by written mandate appoint an authorised representative established in the Union. The mandate shall empower the representative to verify that the EU declaration of conformity and technical documentation have been drawn up and that an appropriate conformity assessment procedure has been carried out; to keep at the disposal of authorities the contact details of the provider, a copy of the EU declaration of conformity, the technical documentation and where applicable the notified-body certificate for 10 years; to provide authorities on reasoned request with all information and documentation necessary to demonstrate conformity; to cooperate with authorities on any action taken in relation to the system; and where applicable to comply with the registration obligations of Article 49(1).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The representative shall terminate the mandate and immediately inform the relevant market surveillance authority and, where applicable, the notified body, where it considers or has reason to consider that the provider acts contrary to its obligations. Application date DEFERRED by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744: the obligations of stand-alone high-risk AI systems under Annex III now apply from 2 December 2027 (previously 2 August 2026), and for AI systems embedded in products covered by the Annex I harmonisation legislation from 2 August 2028 (previously 2 August 2027).

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Before placing a high-risk AI system on the market, verify that it conforms with this Regulation: that the provider carried out the relevant conformity assessment procedure, drew up the technical documentation, that the system bears the required CE marking and is accompanied by the EU declaration of conformity and instructions for use, and that the provider appointed an authorised representative where required. Where there is sufficient reason to consider the system non-conformant, falsified, or accompanied by falsified documentation, do not place it on the market until brought into conformity, and where it presents a risk within the meaning of Article 79(1) inform the provider, the authorised representatives and the market surveillance authorities. Indicate the importer's name, registered trade name or trade mark and address on the system, its packaging or accompanying documentation. Ensure storage and transport conditions do not jeopardise compliance. Keep a copy of the notified-body certificate where applicable, the instructions for use and the EU declaration of conformity for 10 years.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Application date DEFERRED by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744: the obligations of stand-alone high-risk AI systems under Annex III now apply from 2 December 2027 (previously 2 August 2026), and for AI systems embedded in products covered by the Annex I harmonisation legislation from 2 August 2028 (previously 2 August 2027).

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Before making a high-risk AI system available on the market, verify that it bears the required CE marking, is accompanied by a copy of the EU declaration of conformity and instructions for use, and that the provider and where applicable the importer have complied with their obligations under Article 16(b),(c) and Article 23(3). Where there is sufficient reason to consider the system non-conformant, do not make it available until brought into conformity, and where it presents a risk within the meaning of Article 79(1) inform the provider or importer. Ensure storage and transport conditions do not jeopardise compliance. Where a distributor considers or has reason to consider that a system it has made available is non-conformant, take the corrective actions necessary or ensure the provider, importer or relevant operator takes them, and inform authorities as required. Provide competent authorities on reasoned request with all information and documentation regarding the actions taken.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Application date DEFERRED by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744: the obligations of stand-alone high-risk AI systems under Annex III now apply from 2 December 2027 (previously 2 August 2026), and for AI systems embedded in products covered by the Annex I harmonisation legislation from 2 August 2028 (previously 2 August 2027).

controls.title: Responsibilities along the AI value chain

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A distributor, importer, deployer or other third party shall be considered a provider of a high-risk AI system, and assume the provider obligations of Article 16, where it puts its name or trade mark on a high-risk system already placed on the market or put into service; makes a substantial modification to such a system such that it remains high-risk; or modifies the intended purpose of an AI system, including a general-purpose AI system, not classified as high-risk in such a way that it becomes high-risk. Where this occurs, the initial provider shall no longer be considered a provider of that specific system but shall closely cooperate, make available the necessary information and provide the reasonably expected technical access and other assistance, unless it has clearly specified that its system is not to be changed into a high-risk system.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Providers of high-risk systems and third parties supplying AI systems, tools, services, components or processes used in them shall specify their respective roles by written agreement (Article 25(4)); free and open-source tools are excepted. This control is where most misassigned responsibility is found in practice. Application date DEFERRED by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744: the obligations of stand-alone high-risk AI systems under Annex III now apply from 2 December 2027 (previously 2 August 2026), and for AI systems embedded in products covered by the Annex I harmonisation legislation from 2 August 2028 (previously 2 August 2027).

controls.title: Obligations of deployers of high-risk AI systems

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Deployers of high-risk AI systems shall discharge each of the following obligations.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: take appropriate technical and organisational measures to ensure use in accordance with the instructions for use

parts.name: item
parts.prose: assign human oversight to natural persons who have the necessary competence, training and authority, as well as the necessary support

parts.name: item
parts.prose: where the deployer exercises control over input data, ensure that input data is relevant and sufficiently representative in view of the intended purpose

parts.name: item
parts.prose: monitor the operation of the system on the basis of the instructions for use and, where relevant, inform providers in accordance with Article 72

parts.name: item
parts.prose: keep the automatically generated logs to the extent they are under the deployer's control, for a period appropriate to the intended purpose and of at least six months unless provided otherwise in applicable law

parts.name: item
parts.prose: before putting into service or using a high-risk system at the workplace, inform workers' representatives and the affected workers that they will be subject to its use

parts.name: item
parts.prose: where the deployer is a public authority or Union institution, comply with the registration obligations of Article 49

parts.name: item
parts.prose: where applicable, use the information provided under Article 13 to comply with the data protection impact assessment obligation under the GDPR or the Law Enforcement Directive

parts.name: item
parts.prose: where a decision taken on the basis of the system's output concerns a natural person, inform that person that they are subject to its use

parts.name: item
parts.prose: cooperate with the relevant competent authorities on any action taken in relation to the high-risk AI system

parts.name: item
parts.prose: where the deployer identifies a serious incident, immediately inform the provider, then the importer or distributor and the relevant market surveillance authorities (Article 73 applies where the provider cannot be reached)

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: For Annex III(1) post-remote biometric identification in law-enforcement contexts, Article 26(10) additionally requires prior judicial or administrative authorisation and annual reporting; those conditions are separately assessable. Application date DEFERRED by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744: the obligations of stand-alone high-risk AI systems under Annex III now apply from 2 December 2027 (previously 2 August 2026), and for AI systems embedded in products covered by the Annex I harmonisation legislation from 2 August 2028 (previously 2 August 2027).

controls.title: Fundamental rights impact assessment for high-risk AI systems

guidelines.prose: Organisation-defined. Article 27(2) requires a new assessment where any of the described elements changes or is no longer up to date; define the triggers and a periodic review interval.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Before deploying a high-risk AI system referred to in Article 6(2) — excluding systems intended to be used in Annex III(2) critical infrastructure — deployers that are bodies governed by public law, private entities providing public services, and deployers of Annex III(5)(b) and (c) systems (creditworthiness/credit scoring and risk assessment and pricing in life and health insurance) shall perform an assessment of the impact on fundamental rights that the use may produce. The assessment shall describe the deployer's processes in which the system will be used; the period and frequency of intended use; the categories of natural persons and groups likely to be affected; the specific risks of harm to them, taking account of the information given by the provider under Article 13; the human-oversight measures to be implemented; and the measures to be taken if those risks materialise, including internal governance and complaint mechanisms. Notify the market surveillance authority of the results, submitting the filled-out template under Article 27(5), and repeat the assessment when {{ insert: param, aia-27_prm_1 }} occurs.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Where any of the obligations is already met through a data protection impact assessment under the GDPR, the fundamental-rights assessment complements it (Article 27(4)). Deployers may rely on a previously conducted assessment for similar use cases. Application date DEFERRED by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744: the obligations of stand-alone high-risk AI systems under Annex III now apply from 2 December 2027 (previously 2 August 2026), and for AI systems embedded in products covered by the Annex I harmonisation legislation from 2 August 2028 (previously 2 August 2027). Amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744: cross-references between the fundamental-rights impact assessment and the data protection impact assessment are clarified, and the AI Office is to provide an automated template tool.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Before placing the high-risk AI system on the market or putting it into service, follow the applicable conformity assessment procedure. For Annex III(1) biometrics systems, follow either the Annex VI internal-control procedure where harmonised standards or common specifications have been applied, or the Annex VII procedure involving a notified body; where those standards or specifications have not been applied or have been applied only in part, the Annex VII procedure is mandatory. For Annex III(2)-(8) systems, follow the Annex VI internal-control procedure. For systems covered by the Annex I Section A harmonisation legislation, follow the conformity assessment procedure required by that legislation, with this Regulation's requirements forming part of the assessment. Where the system is substantially modified, undergo a new conformity assessment; changes to a system that continues to learn which were pre-determined and assessed at the time of the initial assessment do not constitute a substantial modification.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Application date DEFERRED by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744: the obligations of stand-alone high-risk AI systems under Annex III now apply from 2 December 2027 (previously 2 August 2026), and for AI systems embedded in products covered by the Annex I harmonisation legislation from 2 August 2028 (previously 2 August 2027). Amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, with the amendment applicable from 2 August 2026: bodies already notified under other Union harmonisation legislation apply by 28 January 2028.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Draw up a written machine-readable, physical or electronically signed EU declaration of conformity for each high-risk AI system and keep it at the disposal of the national competent authorities for 10 years after the system has been placed on the market or put into service. The declaration shall identify the system, state that it is in conformity with this Regulation and with any other applicable Union legislation, contain the information set out in Annex V, and be translated into a language required by the Member States in which the system is made available. By drawing it up the provider assumes responsibility for compliance; keep it up to date.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Application date DEFERRED by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744: the obligations of stand-alone high-risk AI systems under Annex III now apply from 2 December 2027 (previously 2 August 2026), and for AI systems embedded in products covered by the Annex I harmonisation legislation from 2 August 2028 (previously 2 August 2027).

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Affix the CE marking visibly, legibly and indelibly to the high-risk AI system or, where that is not possible or warranted by the nature of the system, to its packaging or accompanying documentation. For digitally provided systems, use a digital CE marking only if it can be accessed via the interface from which the system is accessed or via an easily accessible machine-readable code or other electronic means. Where a notified body was involved in the conformity assessment, the marking shall be followed by that body's identification number, which the body itself or the provider on its instructions shall affix.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Application date DEFERRED by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744: the obligations of stand-alone high-risk AI systems under Annex III now apply from 2 December 2027 (previously 2 August 2026), and for AI systems embedded in products covered by the Annex I harmonisation legislation from 2 August 2028 (previously 2 August 2027).

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Before placing on the market or putting into service a high-risk AI system listed in Annex III (other than Annex III(2)), the provider or where applicable the authorised representative shall register itself and its system in the EU database referred to in Article 71. Where a provider has concluded under Article 6(3) that its Annex III system is not high-risk, it shall nevertheless register itself and that system in the EU database. Before putting into service or using a high-risk Annex III system, deployers that are public authorities, Union institutions, bodies, offices or agencies, or persons acting on their behalf, shall register themselves, select the system and register its use.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Application date DEFERRED by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744: the obligations of stand-alone high-risk AI systems under Annex III now apply from 2 December 2027 (previously 2 August 2026), and for AI systems embedded in products covered by the Annex I harmonisation legislation from 2 August 2028 (previously 2 August 2027). Amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, with the amendment applicable from 2 August 2026: Annex VIII Section B registration requirements are reduced (points 7 and 9 deleted). Registration remains required for Annex III systems self-assessed as not high-risk under Article 6(3).

groups.title: Transparency Obligations for Providers and Deployers of Certain AI Systems

controls.title: Transparency obligations for providers and deployers of certain AI systems

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Providers and deployers of the AI systems identified below shall discharge the corresponding transparency obligations. Information shall be provided to the natural persons concerned in a clear and distinguishable manner at the latest at the time of the first interaction or exposure, and shall conform to the accessibility requirements of Directives (EU) 2016/2102 and (EU) 2019/882.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: providers shall ensure that AI systems intended to interact directly with natural persons are designed and developed so that the natural persons concerned are informed that they are interacting with an AI system, unless this is obvious from the point of view of a reasonably well-informed, observant and circumspect natural person taking into account the circumstances and context of use

parts.name: item
parts.prose: providers of AI systems, including general-purpose AI systems, generating synthetic audio, image, video or text content shall ensure the outputs are marked in a machine-readable format and detectable as artificially generated or manipulated, with technical solutions that are effective, interoperable, robust and reliable as far as technically feasible

parts.name: item
parts.prose: deployers of an emotion recognition system or a biometric categorisation system shall inform the natural persons exposed to it of its operation and process personal data in accordance with applicable Union data protection law

parts.name: item
parts.prose: deployers of an AI system that generates or manipulates image, audio or video content constituting a deep fake shall disclose that the content has been artificially generated or manipulated; deployers of an AI system that generates or manipulates text published to inform the public on matters of public interest shall disclose that the text has been artificially generated or manipulated, save where the content has undergone human review or editorial control and a natural or legal person holds editorial responsibility

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Article 50 applies independently of risk classification: a system that is not high-risk may still be fully in scope here. The marking obligation in paragraph 2 does not apply where the AI system performs an assistive function for standard editing or does not substantially alter the input data or its semantics. NOT deferred by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744: the Article 50 transparency obligations remain applicable from 2 August 2026 and are, following the Omnibus, the principal new obligation landing on that date. The machine-readable marking duty in Article 50(2) has a transition to 2 December 2026 for generative systems placed on the market before 2 August 2026 (new Article 111(4)). Article 50(7) retains the Commission's power to act on inadequate codes of practice.

controls.title: Classification of general-purpose AI models as general-purpose AI models with systemic risk

constraints.description: Fixed by Article 51(2) at 10^25 FLOP. The Commission may amend the threshold by delegated act under Article 51(3); verify the currently applicable value before relying on this parameter.
Fixed by Article 52(1): without delay and in any event within two weeks after the requirement is met or it becomes known that it will be met.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Determine whether a general-purpose AI model is to be classified as a general-purpose AI model with systemic risk. A model shall be so classified where it has high-impact capabilities evaluated on the basis of appropriate technical tools and methodologies including indicators and benchmarks, or where, on the basis of a Commission decision, it has capabilities or an impact equivalent to those. A model shall be presumed to have high-impact capabilities where the cumulative amount of computation used for its training measured in floating point operations is greater than {{ insert: param, aia-51_prm_1 }}. Notify the Commission without delay and in any event within {{ insert: param, aia-51_prm_2 }} after the requirement is met or it becomes known that it will be met.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The presumption is rebuttable: a provider may present sufficiently substantiated arguments that its model does not, exceptionally, present systemic risks (Article 52(2)).

groups.title: Obligations for providers of general-purpose AI models

controls.title: Obligations for providers of general-purpose AI models

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Providers of general-purpose AI models shall discharge each of the following obligations.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: draw up and keep up to date the technical documentation of the model, including its training and testing process and the results of its evaluation, containing at least the information set out in Annex XI, for the purpose of providing it on request to the AI Office and the national competent authorities

parts.name: item
parts.prose: draw up, keep up to date and make available information and documentation to providers of AI systems who intend to integrate the model into their AI systems, containing at least the elements set out in Annex XII, enabling them to understand the model's capabilities and limitations and to comply with their own obligations

parts.name: item
parts.prose: put in place a policy to comply with Union law on copyright and related rights, in particular to identify and comply with a reservation of rights expressed under Article 4(3) of Directive (EU) 2019/790

parts.name: item
parts.prose: draw up and make publicly available a sufficiently detailed summary about the content used for training the model, according to the template provided by the AI Office

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Obligations (a) and (b) do not apply to providers of models released under a free and open-source licence that allows access, use, modification and distribution and whose parameters including weights, architecture information and model-usage information are made publicly available — unless the model is a general-purpose AI model with systemic risk (Article 53(2)). Providers established in third countries must appoint an authorised representative under Article 54.

controls.title: Authorised representatives of providers of general-purpose AI models

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Prior to placing a general-purpose AI model on the Union market, a provider established in a third country shall by written mandate appoint an authorised representative established in the Union. The mandate shall empower the representative to verify that the Annex XI technical documentation has been drawn up and that the provider has complied with its Article 53 obligations and, where applicable, Article 55; to keep at the disposal of the AI Office and national competent authorities the Annex XI documentation and the contact details of the provider for 10 years after the model has been placed on the market; to provide on reasoned request all information and documentation necessary to demonstrate compliance; and to cooperate with the AI Office and competent authorities on any action taken in relation to the model.

groups.title: Obligations of providers of general-purpose AI models with systemic risk

controls.title: Obligations of providers of general-purpose AI models with systemic risk

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: In addition to the obligations of Article 53, providers of general-purpose AI models with systemic risk shall discharge each of the following obligations.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: perform model evaluation in accordance with standardised protocols and tools reflecting the state of the art, including conducting and documenting adversarial testing of the model with a view to identifying and mitigating systemic risks

parts.name: item
parts.prose: assess and mitigate possible systemic risks at Union level, including their sources, that may stem from the development, the placing on the market, or the use of the model

parts.name: item
parts.prose: keep track of, document and report without undue delay to the AI Office and, as appropriate, to national competent authorities relevant information about serious incidents and possible corrective measures to address them

parts.name: item
parts.prose: ensure an adequate level of cybersecurity protection for the model and its physical infrastructure

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Providers may rely on codes of practice within the meaning of Article 56 to demonstrate compliance until a harmonised standard is published; providers not adhering to an approved code of practice must demonstrate alternative adequate means of compliance for Commission assessment.

groups.title: Post-Market Monitoring, Information Sharing and Market Surveillance

controls.title: Post-market monitoring by providers and post-market monitoring plan for high-risk AI systems

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Establish and document a post-market monitoring system in a manner proportionate to the nature of the AI technologies and to the risks of the high-risk AI system. The system shall actively and systematically collect, document and analyse relevant data provided by deployers or collected through other sources on the performance of high-risk AI systems throughout their lifetime, and shall allow the provider to evaluate continuous compliance with the requirements of Chapter III Section 2. Where relevant, the analysis shall include interaction with other AI systems. The system shall be based on a post-market monitoring plan forming part of the technical documentation of Annex IV.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: This obligation does not cover sensitive operational data of law-enforcement deployers. For providers already subject to equivalent post-market monitoring obligations under sectoral Union law, the elements may be integrated into those existing systems. The obligation itself is not listed among the provisions the Omnibus amended, and Chapter IX applies from the general date of 2 August 2026. Its subject matter, however, is high-risk AI systems, whose obligations Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 deferred to 2 December 2027 (Annex III) and 2 August 2028 (Annex I). See docs/AMENDMENTS.md: this catalog does not resolve that interaction and records it as an open question rather than asserting a date.

groups.title: Sharing of information on serious incidents

constraints.description: Fixed by Article 73(2): immediately, and in any event not later than 15 days after becoming aware. Not organisation-defined; may not be extended.

params.label: serious-incident reporting deadline (widespread infringement or critical-infrastructure disruption)

constraints.description: Fixed by Article 73(3): not later than two days after becoming aware of that incident.

params.label: serious-incident reporting deadline (death of a person)

constraints.description: Fixed by Article 73(4): immediately after establishing, or on suspecting, a causal relationship, and not later than 10 days after the date of becoming aware.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Report any serious incident to the market surveillance authorities of the Member States where that incident occurred. The report shall be made immediately after the provider has established a causal link, or the reasonable likelihood of a causal link, between the AI system and the serious incident, and in any event not later than {{ insert: param, aia-73_prm_1 }} after becoming aware of the serious incident. Where the serious incident is a widespread infringement, or a serious and irreversible disruption of the management or operation of critical infrastructure, the deadline is {{ insert: param, aia-73_prm_2 }}. In the event of the death of a person, the deadline is {{ insert: param, aia-73_prm_3 }}. Where necessary to ensure timely reporting, an initial incomplete report may be submitted followed by a complete report. Following the report, carry out the necessary investigations, including a risk assessment of the incident and corrective action, without altering the AI system in a way that may affect any subsequent evaluation of the causes.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The reporting obligation is shared: a deployer that identifies a serious incident must immediately inform the provider under Article 26(5), and Article 73 applies to the deployer where the provider cannot be reached. For high-risk systems placed on the market by providers already subject to equivalent incident-reporting obligations under sectoral Union law, reporting is limited to serious incidents within the meaning of Article 3(49)(c). The obligation itself is not listed among the provisions the Omnibus amended, and Chapter IX applies from the general date of 2 August 2026. Its subject matter, however, is serious incidents involving high-risk AI systems, whose obligations Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 deferred. See docs/AMENDMENTS.md: this catalog does not resolve that interaction and records it as an open question rather than asserting a date.

controls.title: Right to lodge a complaint with a market surveillance authority

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Any natural or legal person having grounds to consider that there has been an infringement of this Regulation may submit a complaint to the relevant market surveillance authority. Establish and document the organisation's process for receiving, routing and responding to such complaints and to authority follow-up.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Assessable as an organisational readiness control: the right belongs to third parties, but the ability to respond is the operator's.

controls.title: Right to explanation of individual decision-making

guidelines.prose: Organisation-defined. Article 86 fixes no deadline; select one consistent with the organisation's obligations under applicable Union data protection law and with any national implementing rules.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Where a decision is taken by the deployer on the basis of output from a high-risk AI system listed in Annex III — with the exception of systems listed under Annex III(2) — and that decision produces legal effects or similarly significantly affects a person in a way they consider to have an adverse impact on their health, safety or fundamental rights, provide that affected person, on request and within {{ insert: param, aia-86_prm_1 }}, with clear and meaningful explanations of the role of the AI system in the decision-making procedure and of the main elements of the decision taken.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The right does not apply where exceptions or restrictions follow from Union or national law in compliance with Union law. Where Union law already provides an equivalent right to explanation, Article 86 applies only in so far as that right is not already provided. The right attaches to decisions taken on the basis of output from an Annex III high-risk AI system. Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 deferred the Annex III high-risk obligations to 2 December 2027 while Chapter IX continues to apply from 2 August 2026; this catalog records that interaction as unresolved rather than asserting a date. See docs/AMENDMENTS.md.

params.label: maximum fine — Article 5 prohibited practices
values: EUR 35 000 000 or 7 % of total worldwide annual turnover for the preceding financial year

params.label: maximum fine — other operator or notified-body obligations
values: EUR 15 000 000 or 3 % of total worldwide annual turnover for the preceding financial year

params.label: maximum fine — incorrect, incomplete or misleading information
values: EUR 7 500 000 or 1 % of total worldwide annual turnover for the preceding financial year

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Non-compliance is subject to administrative fines laid down by the Member States, which shall be effective, proportionate and dissuasive and shall take into account the interests of SMEs including start-ups and their economic viability. Non-compliance with the prohibition of the AI practices referred to in Article 5 is subject to administrative fines of up to {{ insert: param, aia-99_prm_1 }}. Non-compliance with any other provision related to operators or notified bodies, other than Article 5, is subject to administrative fines of up to {{ insert: param, aia-99_prm_2 }}. The supply of incorrect, incomplete or misleading information to notified bodies or national competent authorities in reply to a request is subject to administrative fines of up to {{ insert: param, aia-99_prm_3 }}. Where the offender is an undertaking, the ceiling is the higher of the fixed amount and the applicable percentage of worldwide annual turnover. For SMEs including start-ups, and for small mid-cap companies under Article 99(6a), the applicable ceiling is the lower of the percentage and the fixed amount.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Included so that assessment findings can be weighted by exposure. Chapter XII applies from 2 August 2025, with the exception of Article 101 (fines for providers of general-purpose AI models), which applies from the general application date. Separate regimes apply to Union institutions (Article 100) and to providers of general-purpose AI models (Article 101); neither is included in this catalog release. Amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 with effect from 27 July 2026: Article 99(1) now also requires Member States to provide non-monetary enforcement measures, and a new Article 99(6a) caps fines for small mid-cap companies at the lower of the applicable percentage and the applicable fixed amount. The Omnibus also added AI Office enforcement powers over general-purpose AI systems and very large online platforms (Articles 75, 75a-75d) applicable from 2 August 2026.

resources.description: The eight Annex III use-case areas that make an AI system high-risk under Article 6(2).

resources.description: The minimum content of the technical documentation required by Article 11.

resources.title: Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (Digital Omnibus on AI) — amending Regulation (EU) 2024/1689
resources.description: Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 8 July 2026 amending Regulations (EU) 2024/1689, (EU) 2018/1139 and (EU) 2023/1230. Published in the Official Journal on 24 July 2026; entered into force on 27 July 2026. It rewrote Article 113, deferring the stand-alone Annex III high-risk obligations to 2 December 2027 and the Annex I embedded obligations to 2 August 2028, inserted two new prohibitions into Article 5(1) applicable from 2 December 2026, inserted Article 4a, and softened Article 4.
